jurisdiction.name: Italy
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Italy was the first EU country to adopt a general national AI law: Law 132/2025, in force since 10 October 2025, sets principles for AI use across sectors, creates a deepfake offence, and names the Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as national AI authorities. Two 2026 legislative decrees under that law cover police use of AI and liability, and the EU AI Act's authorities, fines, sandbox and training, with AI clauses also in the public contracts code and the workplace transparency decree. National policy rests on the 2024-2026 AI strategy (replacing the 2022-2024 programme) and AgID's three-year IT plan for public administration, with draft AgID guidelines on adopting, buying and developing AI in the public sector and ministry documents on AI at work, in schools and in defence. The data protection authority (Garante) is among the most active AI enforcers in Europe, with orders and fines against ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Replika, Clearview AI, Character.AI and delivery platforms' algorithms, while the competition authority, the communications regulator, the Bank of Italy and IVASS have added AI decisions and communications.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 11 October 2026 and covers national law, the national government and ministries, and regulators. Regional and city documents were not reviewed systematically, in line with the project's rule for Italy; regional AI laws and rules found in later searches of official regional sources are recorded. European Union and Council of Europe instruments are shown through the regional files. The decree implementing the EU AI Act enters into force on 23 October 2026, so it is shown as published but not yet in force. The data protection authority's 2024 fine on OpenAI was annulled by a court in 2026 and is shown as repealed. Four documents are recorded as located only; their full text is not yet verified from the official text.

It includes a monitoring system with quantitative indicators and a chapter on the regulatory context and the authorities needed to supervise the EU AI Act nationally.

instruments.scope: Research, testing, development, adoption and use of AI systems and models in Italy; to be interpreted and applied consistently with Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
instruments.summary: Italy's framework AI law (28 articles) sets human-centric principles for AI, requires parental consent for children under 14 to access AI and allows 14-17-year-olds to consent themselves, and adds sector rules for health, work (employers must inform workers of AI use), intellectual professions (AI only as support, with disclosure to clients), public administration (AI only supports decisions, with the official keeping responsibility) and justice. Article 20 designates the Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) as AI notifying authority and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as market surveillance authority and single point of contact under the EU AI Act, without prejudice to the Bank of Italy, CONSOB and IVASS; article 19 sets the national AI strategy process and a coordination committee, and article 23 authorises up to EUR 1 billion of equity investment in AI, cybersecurity and quantum companies. It protects only human-authored works under copyright law (art. 25), creates the offence of unlawful dissemination of AI-generated or altered content (deepfakes, art. 612-quater c.p., 1-5 years) and an aggravating circumstance for crimes committed with AI (art. 26), and delegates the Government to adapt national law to the AI Act and regulate unlawful AI uses within 12 months (arts. 16 and 24).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Italy's horizontal national AI law; designates the national AI Act authorities (AgID, ACN) and is the legal basis for the implementing legislative decrees.

instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Italy (Council of Ministers); issued by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Published in GU Serie Generale n. 214 of 15 September 2026 and in force 30 September 2026, adopted under the delegation in art. 24(3)-(5) of Law 132/2025 (scheme approved preliminarily by the Council of Ministers on 10 June 2026 - Atto del Governo n. 418 - and finally on 4 August 2026, after opinions of the Garante, the Conferenza unificata (20 July 2026) and the parliamentary committees, as recited in the preamble). Police AI systems already in use must be made compliant within one year (art. 21).
instruments.scope: Use of AI systems by Italian police forces; criminal offences and corporate liability involving AI; civil damages actions for harm caused by AI systems
instruments.summary: Regulates the research, testing, training and use of AI systems by the police forces, including biometric categorisation, real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces only for the AI Act's permitted purposes (with a new art. 359-ter c.p.p.), fundamental-rights impact assessments, logging and retrospective facial recognition. It creates the offence of failing to adopt security or human-oversight measures for high-risk AI systems, or unlawfully altering them (art. 437-bis c.p.), and makes companies liable under D.Lgs. 231/2001 for that offence and for deepfake dissemination (art. 612-quater c.p.). For civil claims it provides access to evidence, a rebuttable presumption of causation where harm follows a breach of the AI Act, says AI Act conformity does not by itself exclude liability, and gives a right to ask about the defendant's liability insurance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First implementing decree of Law 132/2025; national rules on police use of AI and on criminal and civil liability for AI systems.

instruments.summary: Italy's AI Act implementing decree: confirms AgID as notifying authority and ACN as market surveillance authority and single point of contact, makes the Bank of Italy, CONSOB and IVASS market surveillance authorities for high-risk AI in banking, investment and insurance services and the Garante for the cases in AI Act art. 74(8), and sets their supervisory, inspection, registration (ACN for Annex III point 2 systems) and sanctioning powers. It sets administrative fines of up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover for prohibited practices and up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other breaches, and establishes the Italian AI regulatory sandbox under AI Act art. 57 run by AgID and ACN. Chapter III adds AI training measures for students, teachers, adults, public employees, justice staff, professionals and health workers, requires that final employment decisions taken with AI be made by a person, and protects AI training data, algorithms and methods as trade secrets (art. 98(1-bis) of the industrial property code).

instruments.scope: Contracting authorities and awarding entities (stazioni appaltanti and enti concedenti); AI-relevant provision is art. 30
instruments.summary: Italy's public procurement code; article 30 tells contracting authorities to automate their activities where possible, including with artificial intelligence and distributed-ledger technologies. When buying or developing such solutions they must secure the source code and documentation needed to understand how they work and include maintenance clauses to correct errors. Automated decisions must respect knowability and comprehensibility, non-exclusivity of the algorithmic decision (meaningful human control) and algorithmic non-discrimination, and public administrations must publish the list of the technological solutions they use in the 'Amministrazione trasparente' section of their websites.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with explicit AI provisions for public procurement and automated decisions by contracting authorities.

instruments.english_title: Veneto Regional Government Resolution No. 1467 of 20 November 2025 approving the Rules for the adoption and use of AI systems and models in the Veneto Region
instruments.current_status: Adopted 20 November 2025; published in BUR Veneto n. 158 of 28 November 2025. Binding on the regional administration's structures.
instruments.summary: Approves the rules governing AI in Veneto's regional administrative procedures and activities: general principles, prohibitions drawn from the AI Act and national law, and a three-level governance (coordination table, AI Competence Center within the ICT Directorate, AI referents in each Area). Every AI project needs a formal risk assessment; a public register of AI systems is to be kept under 'Amministrazione trasparente', and offices must declare use of generative AI in drafting acts. Annexes: glossary and rules of conduct.

instruments.summary: Provincial resolution approving practical guidelines, drafted in line with the AI Act and GDPR, for all employees and authorised collaborators using AI for the Province, plus an action plan of priority AI interventions. instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Culture - Directorate-General for Cinema and Audiovisual
instruments.current_status: Issued 24 April 2025 by the Directorate-General for Cinema and Audiovisual (directorial decree rep. 1601, annex 1); conditions eligibility for the tax credit.
instruments.summary: Directorial guidance interpreting art. 7(6) of Ministerial Decree 10 July 2024 n. 225 (tax credit for national audiovisual production): to be eligible, productions' contracts must let authors and performers refuse AI use of their work, image or performance; training generative models to create 'digital replicas' requires the actor's explicit consent and equivalent pay; artists' image, voice or text may not be sold to AI firms to build general-purpose models; artists must be told how their performance is used in AI; clauses replacing human authorship with AI are inadmissible, and side letters altering these terms make the project ineligible.

instruments.english_title: Apulia Regional Law No. 4 of 14 April 2025 - Measures to promote open innovation and artificial intelligence, and miscellaneous provisions
instruments.current_status: Published in the Bollettino Ufficiale della Regione Puglia n. 2 straordinario of 18 April 2025; declared urgent, it entered into force on the day of publication (art. 15(1)).
instruments.summary: Regional law whose Chapter I ('Disposizioni in materia di innovazione aperta e intelligenza artificiale') commits the Region to support the diffusion of AI as a development tool, in line with Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (art. 1), and to promote AI use in local and regional public administration through networks of digital transition officers (art. 8). Art. 9 gives a statutory basis to the Regional Competence Centre for AI in public administration set up by DGR 1488/2023, which defines the Region's AI strategy for its administration, studies and monitors AI systems, drafts guidelines and tests AI tools; art. 10 provides for support to AI adoption by SMEs, including training, research projects, awareness campaigns and AI courses, and the innovation platform must give users information to make informed choices about AI-based services (art. 4).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regional law of Apulia promoting AI.
instruments.evidence_reference: BURP PDF read 2026-11-05: title 'Misure di promozione in materia di innovazione aperta e intelligenza artificiale e disposizioni varie', 'n. 4' of 14 April 2025, 'Bollettino Ufficiale della Regione Puglia, n. 2 straordinario, del 18 aprile 2025'; art. 9 'Centro di competenza regionale per l'intelligenza artificiale nella pubblica amministrazione'; art. 15(1) 'entra in vigore il giorno stesso della sua pubblicazione sul Bollettino ufficiale della Regione'. Chapter II amends unrelated regional laws.

instruments.official_title: Legge regionale 2 febbraio 2026, n. 4 - Disposizioni concernenti l'impiego di sistemi di intelligenza artificiale in ambito regionale
instruments.english_title: Calabria Regional Law No. 4 of 2 February 2026 - Provisions on the use of artificial intelligence systems in the regional sphere
instruments.current_status: Published in BURC n. 22 of 2 February 2026. The coordinated text contains no entry-into-force clause, so no effective date is shown. The operating regulation of the Regional AI Office (Regolamento regionale n. 5/2026) was adopted in June 2026 under this law.
instruments.summary: Regional AI law governing the use of AI systems in the Calabrian regional public administration. It adopts the AI Act definition and requires respect for data protection and cybersecurity rules and human review based on transparency, accountability and equity. It mandates a health-sector AI pilot programme (waiting lists, diagnostics and screening, home monitoring) within 90 days and a voluntary Regional AI Register of developers (by regulation within 180 days). It also creates a Regional AI Office within the digital transition department with three unpaid experts (two appointed by the Giunta, one by the Council), which reports annually to the Giunta and the Council, plus an evaluation clause requiring reports to the Council.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regional AI law of Calabria.
instruments.evidence_reference: Calabria Regional Council coordinated text read 2026-11-05: 'Legge regionale 2 febbraio 2026, n. 4', title 'Disposizioni concernenti l'impiego di sistemi di intelligenza artificiale in ambito regionale', 'BURC n. 22 del 2 febbraio 2026'; arts. 4 (health pilot), 5 (Registro regionale IA), 6 (Ufficio regionale IA). Corroborated by Giunta DGR n. 355 of 25 June 2026 (regione.calabria.it).

instruments.english_title: Calabria Regional Regulation No. 5 of 2026 - Regulation on the operation of the Regional Office for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.current_status: Approved by the Giunta on 25 June 2026 (DGR n. 355) and published in BURC n. 138 of 3 July 2026; it takes effect the day after publication.
instruments.summary: Implements Regional Law 4/2026 by setting how the Regional AI Office operates within the digital transition department in close collaboration with the Regional Digital Transition Officer. The Office assesses regional AI systems against AI Act risk categories (with attention to prohibited and high-risk systems), runs pilots and training, issues operational guidelines and recommendations, and handles AI Act information duties including registration of high-risk systems in the EU database; procurement of AI systems must comply with the Office's recommendations, based on AgID procurement guidelines. It reports annually to the Giunta (first report by 31 January 2027).

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Italy were searched, including the national legislation database, the government and its ministries, the digital agency, the Department for Digital Transformation and the regulators. No qualifying material was found for standards or international instruments; EU and Council of Europe instruments are shown through the regional files. A prime ministerial decree of 6 May 2026 and some ministry documents are listed as leads or only located, and Legislative Decree 179/2026 enters into force on 2026-10-23.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-11 in three parts (I1 law via Normattiva full-text search, 94 acts screened; I2 government incl. ministry-level search, AgID and the Department for Digital Transformation; I3 regulators), national level only per PROTOCOL §6. Run in parallel with NLD on separate branches. No interruption. The three earlier records were re-checked and fixed (Law 132/2025 with in-force date and amendments; 2024-2026 strategy retitled and dated 2024-07-22; Piano triennale record now the 2026 update approved by DPCM 2025-09-04, with the 2024 original and 2025 update as superseded). EU and CoE instruments are attached via the regional files. Merge: duplicate G7 'SBOM for AI' record from I2 dropped in favour of I3's; the 2023 NCSC/CISA-led 'Guidelines for secure AI system development' moved to leads (ACN co-signatory only). D.Lgs. 179/2026 enters into force 2026-10-23 (lifecycle published; update after that date). Garante decision of 2 Nov 2024 against OpenAI recorded as repealed: the Garante removed it after the Court of Rome upheld OpenAI's appeal (judgment 4153/2026); text unreadable, located only. Replika fine amount redacted in the published decision. Access: presidenza.governo.it (DPCM 6 May 2026: reset/503, lead), mim.gov.it and unica.istruzione.gov.it 403 (DM 166 located only), INPS directive page script-rendered (located only), ia.italia.it reset, acn.gov.it AI guidelines page 403. CONSOB AI Quaderni FinTech carry an authors'-views disclaimer and are not recorded. standards, international: no material found.
